To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the binding of three fermions in a medium with short-range interactions is possible only in the case where the two-fermon pair binding is absent (Borromean state), while the two-fermi binding is suppressed at high phase space occupation (Mott effect) and is absent at the critical density (Motts effect).

the formation of two- and three-particle bound systems in a medium is governed by the competition between the Pauli blocking effect (Pauli exclusion principle) and Bose enhancement of fermions (Bose-Einstein statistics) in the medium.

1) the binding energy of two-fermionic bound states in a Fermi sea decreases with increasing density due to Pauli blocking; 2) three-fermionic Borromean bound states can be realized in a Fermi gas only at high phase space occupation; 3) the binding energy for the three-fermions bound states is enhanced due to the Bose enhancement of the fermion pairs.
